processing.reason: The historical fault in PR #130786 is not a value-level miscompilation. `EarlyOtherwiseBranch` created its synthesized `eq_switch` with `BasicBlockData::new(...)`, whose old `is_cleanup: false` default was wrong when the matched parent block was a cleanup block. The observable historical failure is MIR validation rejecting a cleanup->normal edge (`cleanup true -> false`) and thus an ICE (`Fixes #130769`), not a different computed result. The corrected pass conservatively returns `None` for `bbs[parent].is_cleanup`, and the regression test itself states “NB: This transform is not happening currently.” Ordinary Rust source has no observable notion of a MIR basic block’s `is_cleanup` bit, and cleanup blocks only run on unwind. A source-level pair would therefore either compute identical values on every defined input or would require inventing a separate value-changing rewrite (e.g. changing branches/returns), which the task explicitly forbids. Since both functions must pass Miri and produce different values, no source-grounded counterexample pair exists for this invariant/ICE fix; fabricating one would not encode the actual historical wrong transformation.

analysis.summary: Historical fix for an ICE in `EarlyOtherwiseBranch`: when the pass rewrites a parent `SwitchInt` and creates a new branch block (`eq_switch`), that new block must inherit `is_cleanup` from the parent. The old constructor `BasicBlockData::new(terminator)` always set `is_cleanup: false`, so a sub-block created under a cleanup BB became a normal BB, producing a cleanup->normal edge that violates MIR unwind invariants. The PR makes `is_cleanup` an explicit `BasicBlockData::new` argument, propagates `bbs[parent].is_cleanup` to the new block (and `caller_body[block].is_cleanup` in `inline.rs`), and conservatively bails out of the pass for cleanup parents. It also extends the pass to a no-hoist case (zero-statement child block switching directly on `Operand::Copy(place)`).
analysis.originalLogic: In the pre-fix pass, `EarlyOtherwiseBranch` matched a parent `SwitchInt` on a discriminant followed by per-value child `SwitchInt`s on a second place, then created a new block `eq_switch` with `let eq_switch = BasicBlockData::new(Some(Terminator { ... }));`. The old `BasicBlockData::new(terminator)` hard-coded `is_cleanup: false`. The pass did not check whether the parent BB was itself a cleanup block, so when the matched parent was a cleanup BB the newly inserted `eq_switch` was marked normal, while the original cleanup region required all sub-blocks to remain cleanup.
analysis.incorrectTransformation: The historically incorrect rewrite is: create the new `eq_switch` BasicBlockData with the default `is_cleanup: false` even though the parent block it is derived from has `is_cleanup == true`. In MIR terms it turned a cleanup BB's successor into a non-cleanup BB, i.e. a normal edge out of cleanup, instead of copying the parent's cleanup status. This is not the value-level branch-to-comparison rewrite itself (which is legal when types/patterns agree); the faulty dimension is the `is_cleanup` bit of the newly created sub-BB. A two-variant comparison is: same matched nested `SwitchInt` pattern in a normal parent versus in a cleanup/unwind parent; the old pass produced a normal `eq_switch` in both, the corrected behavior either marks it cleanup or (currently) skips the transformation.
analysis.inputDomain: MIR for functions containing nested enum matches whose payloads need drop, so the MIR builder emits unwind/cleanup blocks, e.g. `Poll<Result<Option<Vec<u8>>, u8>>` (from the http-body `poll` ICE) and `Option<Option<Option<T>>>`. The candidate must expose a parent `SwitchInt` whose `otherwise` is empty/unreachable and whose child arm is a `SwitchInt` on a second place of the same type. Unwind strategy must be available (`PanicStrategy::Unwind` / `needs-unwind`); otherwise no cleanup BB is present.
analysis.trigger: The pass evaluates a candidate parent BB where `bbs[parent].is_cleanup == true` (a cleanup block whose terminator still matches the otherwise-branch pattern). Before the fix, `evaluate_candidate` did not reject or re-tag such a parent, so the generated `eq_switch` sub-block was created non-cleanup.
preconditions: Unwinding enabled, so MIR contains cleanup BBs (needs-unwind / PanicStrategy::Unwind).
The matched parent BB is a cleanup block (is_cleanup true), typically reached via an unwind edge such as a drop's unwind target.
The parent terminator is SwitchInt on a discriminant with an empty/unreachable otherwise branch.
A child arm is a SwitchInt on a child place of the same type, matching the pass's candidate shape so the pass attempts the rewrite.
pitfalls: Constructing a new MIR BasicBlockData with a default `is_cleanup: false` under a cleanup parent creates an illegal cleanup->normal edge and trips mir-opt validation ('violates unwind invariants (cleanup true -> false)').
The cleanup status of a newly synthesized sub-block is a separate correctness dimension from whether the value rewrite (discriminant comparison) is legal; both must be checked.

The fix also needed the unwind return block in `inline.rs` to inherit `caller_body[block].is_cleanup`, showing the invariant applies to any newly created block that is inserted into an existing region.

The pass now distinguishes hoisting the second discriminant (one-statement child) from switching directly on `Operand::Copy(child_place)` (zero-statement child); do not conflate the hoist-UB guard (otherwise must be empty/unreachable) with the cleanup-status invariant.
The `unwind` regression test notes 'This transform is not happening currently', so absence of a new comparison in a cleanup parent is expected behavior, not a missed optimization bug.
analysis.testStrategy: Add MIR-opt regression tests gated with `//@ test-mir-pass: EarlyOtherwiseBranch`, `//@ compile-flags: -Zmir-enable-passes=+GVN,+SimplifyLocals-after-value-numbering`, and `//@ needs-unwind`. Use nested-enum matches whose payloads drop (e.g. `Poll<Result<Option<Vec<u8>>, u8>>`, `Option<Option<Option<T>>>`) and `// EMIT_MIR ...EarlyOtherwiseBranch.diff`. CHECK that the unwind target block is emitted as a cleanup block, e.g. `[[PARENT_UNWIND_BB]] (cleanup):` followed by `CHECK-NEXT: switchInt`, so the cleanup->normal-edge invariant is exercised. Also add negative/shape tests (`opt5_failed` with mismatched arm, `opt5_failed_type` with differing child type) that CHECK-NOT: `Ne(` to confirm the pass bails out, and a positive `opt5` test that checks the hoisted `CMP_LOCAL = Ne(...)` rewrite. No compiler was built here; these are test-design inferences from the supplied diffs.
